questions.q: What does quorum determine in a Windows Server Failover Cluster?
options: The backup schedule for the FCI's databases
How much disk space each node is allowed to use
The SQL Server edition licensed on each node
Whether enough nodes are communicating to safely keep running cluster resources, especially during a network partition
questions.explain: Quorum is the mechanism that decides which group of nodes, if the cluster splits, is allowed to keep running.

questions.q: In the node majority quorum model, what's required for the cluster to keep running?
options: A shared witness disk is always mandatory
Exactly one node must be online
More than half of the nodes must be online and able to communicate
All nodes must be online with zero tolerance for any being down
questions.explain: Node majority gives each node one vote and requires a majority (more than half) to remain online.

questions.q: What role does a cloud witness play in quorum, per this lesson?
options: It replaces the need for any cluster nodes at all
It only works for clusters with an odd number of nodes
It automatically restores the database after a failover
It acts as a tie-breaking vote using an Azure Storage account, useful for clusters spanning sites
questions.explain: Cloud witness is a modern alternative to a physical witness disk, useful when a shared disk isn't practical across sites.

questions.q: What specific problem does quorum exist to prevent?
options: SQL Server licensing violations
Running out of disk space on the witness disk
Slow query performance on the active node
Split-brain — isolated groups of nodes each believing they should be active and both trying to own the shared storage
questions.explain: Quorum guarantees at most one side of a network partition can ever hold a majority, making split-brain structurally impossible.

questions.q: A four-node cluster splits into two groups of two nodes each, with no witness. What does quorum say should happen?
options: The cluster automatically adds a fifth node to break the tie
Neither group holds a majority, so cluster resources stop on both sides — even though some nodes are healthy
Both groups keep running independently since they're evenly split
The group with the lower IP address automatically wins
questions.explain: With no majority possible in an even split and no tie-breaking witness, quorum is lost on both sides, and cluster resources stop — the safe outcome that avoids split-brain.
